+// executeDestroyTargetPermanentEffect implements the
+// triggered_single_target_destroy primitive (ticket
+// engine.auto-triggered-single-target-destroy-cd8f155f56, Ragnarok,
+// Divine Deliverance class): "When Ragnarok dies, destroy target
+// permanent and return target nonlegendary permanent card from your
+// graveyard to the battlefield." Unlike the qualified destroy variants
+// above (excluding subtypes, mana-value-gated, etc.), this is the plain,
+// unconditional single-target destroy clause of a TRIGGERED ability —
+// the same DestroyTarget helper every other destroy primitive in this
+// file uses, called once per target. A target that isn't a card or is
+// no longer on the battlefield (already gone by resolution time, Rule
+// 608.2b) is skipped rather than failing the whole effect, mirroring
+// executeDestroyExcludingSubtypesEffect's per-target no-op convention
+// just above.
+func (gs *GameState) executeDestroyTargetPermanentEffect(targets []Target) error {
+	for _, target := range targets {
+		if !target.IsCard || target.CardID == "" {
+			continue
+		}
+		card, err := gs.Battlefield.GetCard(target.CardID)
+		if err != nil || card == nil {
+			continue
+		}
+		if err := DestroyTarget(Target{IsCard: true, CardID: card.ID}, gs); err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
 // subtypesFromEffectValue normalizes an effect_value subtype list (parsed
 // from JSON, so a []interface{} of strings) into a []string. Returns nil
 // for any other shape or an empty/absent value, mirroring

@@ -0,0 +1,40 @@
+package game
+
+import "testing"
+
+// Ticket engine.auto-triggered-single-target-destroy-cd8f155f56:
+// executeDestroyTargetPermanentEffect must destroy a single targeted
+// permanent (Ragnarok, Divine Deliverance's "When Ragnarok dies, destroy
+// target permanent" clause) — moving it off the battlefield and into its
+// owner's graveyard.
+func TestExecuteDestroyTargetPermanentEffect_TriggeredSingleTarget(t *testing.T) {
+	gs := NewGame("P0", "P1", false)
+
+	target := NewCreature("Ragnarok Prey", ManaCost{}, 2, 2, 1)
+	target.Owner, target.Controller = 1, 1
+	gs.Battlefield.AddCard(target)
+
+	if err := gs.executeDestroyTargetPermanentEffect([]Target{{IsCard: true, CardID: target.ID}}); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("executeDestroyTargetPermanentEffect returned error: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	if _, err := gs.Battlefield.GetCard(target.ID); err == nil {
+		t.Fatalf("expected target removed from battlefield after destroy")
+	}
+	if _, err := gs.Players[1].Graveyard.RemoveCard(target.ID); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("expected destroyed target to be in owner's graveyard: %v", err)
+	}
+}
+
+// A non-card target (or no targets at all) must be a no-op, not an error —
+// mirrors the no-target no-op convention used throughout ability_effects.go.
+func TestExecuteDestroyTargetPermanentEffect_NoTargetIsNoOp(t *testing.T) {
+	gs := NewGame("P0", "P1", false)
+
+	if err := gs.executeDestroyTargetPermanentEffect(nil); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("expected nil-target no-op, got error: %v", err)
+	}
+	if err := gs.executeDestroyTargetPermanentEffect([]Target{{IsCard: false, PlayerIdx: 0}}); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("expected non-card target no-op, got error: %v", err)
+	}
+}
